subject: gecko climbing scaled to humans
title: What If You Could Climb Walls Like a Gecko?

scenes.text: What if you could climb walls like a gecko? Sticky hands wouldn't come close to enough.
Cambridge researchers compared sticky feet across 225 climbing species, from tiny mites up to geckos.
Size changes everything. Mites need about 200 times less of their body for sticky pads than geckos do.
Scale it up to you, and sticky pads would have to cover about 40 percent of your whole body.
That's roughly 80 percent of your front. Put it all on your feet, and you'd need European shoe size 145.
Geckos sit near the size limit for this trick. So engineers cheat: Stanford's gecko pads hold about 200 pounds.

description:
What if you could climb walls like a gecko? A University of Cambridge study of 225 climbing species (PNAS, 2016) found a human would need adhesive pads covering about 40% of the body, roughly 80% of the front, or feet in European shoe size 145; mites use about 200 times less of their body surface for pads than geckos.
Geckos are near the size limit for adhesive climbing, but Stanford's gecko-inspired hand pads can support about 200 pounds.
